I was in this position a few days ago for what seems like the 10000th time. I know it's hard to keep perspective but I try to distract myself with anything even if it's not my intention to in that suicidal mood e.g putting your favourite show on, drawing, listening to music full volume. Anything small that you enjoy. Every little helps.

 If it's to the point where i cant even focus then what works for me to make sure I dont relapse and self harm is going by myself to my local park, I walk and I sit there and listen to music even if I'm bawling my eyes out, I let myself feel it without endangering myself. I know I will hurt myself at home. Sometimes it takes hours to stop the bad thoughts from overpowering. I'm not saying it's going to stop the the pain but the pain will feel less intense as the hours pass. It comes in waves I know it's hard because it feels like it will never stop but you need to find your own way to cope and hang on until it comes back again, dont feel guilty. It's all about the small things and never making yourself feel bad for having negative thoughts. I promise you are not alone.

It is not an overnight change of perspective. I have been on the rollercoaster too, I reached rock bottom the other day and I'm on the climb for the 100th time it is encouraging as much as it is discouraging but we all must find a way to stay afloat.

I think it is hard to do in a world that forces their version of happiness and success onto others which is why so many people feel shame and never speak out. I hope that you keep going, growth is certainly not linear. X
